# Normalization {.tabset}

We create a subset of control barcodes that should not change in abundance between samples.
These barcodes are typically non-targeting controls or they target genes that are not involved in survival/proliferation.

```{r}
use.for.norm <- logical(nrow(y))
norm.features <- character(0)
```

:BEGIN barcodes
We add a pre-defined set of control barcodes:

```{r}
norm.barcodes <- <%= NORM_BARCODES %>
use.for.norm.barcodes <- rownames(y) %in% unlist(norm.barcodes)
summary(use.for.norm.barcodes)
use.for.norm[use.for.norm.barcodes] <- TRUE
norm.features <- c(norm.features, names(norm.barcodes))
```
:END

:BEGIN genes
We add all barcodes associated with a pre-defined set of control genes:

```{r}
norm.genes <- <%= NORM_GENES %>
use.for.norm.genes <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[y$genes$origin, <%= NORM_GENE_FIELD %>] %in% unlist(norm.genes)
summary(use.for.norm.genes)
use.for.norm[use.for.norm.genes] <- TRUE 
norm.features <- c(norm.features, names(norm.genes))
```
:END

:BEGIN types
We add control barcodes based on the row annotation in the `SummarizedExperiment`:

```{r}
norm.types <- <%= NORM_TYPES %>
use.for.norm.types <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(se)[y$genes$origin, <%= NORM_TYPE_FIELD %>] %in% norm.types
summary(use.for.norm.types)
use.for.norm[use.for.norm.types] <- TRUE
norm.features <- c(norm.features, norm.types)
```
:END

We look at the total number of control barcodes:

```{r}
stopifnot(any(use.for.norm)) # make sure we have at least some controls.
norm.features <- paste(norm.features, collapse=', ')
summary(use.for.norm)
```

:BEGIN tmm
We define a normalization factor for each sample with the TMM method across all control barcodes.
The assumption is that most of these barcodes not exhibit any differences between samples;
any systematic differences across many barcodes are assumed to be technical and removed.

```{r}
# Preserve the library sizes as normalization factors should only be
# interpreted in the context of the library sizes used to compute them.
ysub <- edgeR::normLibSizes(y[use.for.norm,,keep.lib.sizes=TRUE])
stopifnot(identical(ysub$samples$lib.size, y$sample$lib.size))

y$samples$norm.factors <- ysub$samples$norm.factors
norm.meta <- paste0('TMM on controls (', norm.features, ')')
head(y$samples)
```

The TMM normalization factors account for composition biases that are not reflected in the relative library sizes.
Specifically, composition biases are introduced when upregulation of some genes in one sample reduces the sequencing resources available for other genes.
This shifts the log-fold changes and causes spurious DE when that sample is compared to other samples with less upregulation.
`r BiocStyle::Biocpkg("edgeR")` handles this by computing effective library sizes (`lib.size` scaled by `norm.factors`),
which represent the combined effect of library size differences and composition biases.

```{r}
nf <- y$samples$norm.factors
names(nf) <- colnames(y)
nf <- sort(nf)
head(nf) # samples with lowest factors have more upregulated genes
tail(nf) # samples with highest factors have fewer upregulated genes
```
:END

:BEGIN lib
We define a normalization factor for each sample based on the sequencing depth (i.e., total counts) across all control barcodes.
Our assumption is that the control barcodes should not change in abundance across samples,
thus any difference in coverage is technical in nature and should be normalized away via scaling.

```{r, fig.wide=TRUE}
# The actual scaling applied to each library is proportional to the effective
# library size, i.e., the product of the library size and normalization factor.
# So, if we want to scale by the sum of control counts, we define the
# normalization factors as the ratio to the library sizes.
ratio <- colSums(y$counts[use.for.norm,,drop=FALSE])/y$samples$lib.size

# Scaled to a geometric mean of 1 to preserve the scale of the library sizes. 
y$samples$norm.factors <- ratio/exp(mean(log(ratio)))

norm.meta <- paste0('library size on controls (', norm.features, ')')
head(y$samples)
```
:END 

We inspect the normalization results by creating MD (mean-difference) plots.
Ideally, the log-fold changes for most control barcodes should be centered around zero if the normalization was successful.

```{r plot-md-norm, results="asis"}
y.cpm <- edgeR::cpm(y, log=TRUE, prior.count=3)

# Avoid creating too many plots, otherwise the compiled report is too big.
for (i in seq_len(min(9, ncol(y.cpm)))) {
    cat(paste0("\n\n## ", i, " {-}\n"))
    limma::plotMD(y.cpm, column=i, status=as.integer(use.for.norm))
    abline(h=0, col='red', lty=2)
}
```
